subject: Session billing exceptions & long-prompt treatment for Acme Health
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify how you bill for very long prompts / streaming sessions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team is excited about the throughput and latency. Before we sign the pilot SOW, procurement raised a couple of billing questions that I want to get clarified so we don't get surprises once the pilot goes live. Two narrow asks:

1) For very long prompts (we often send a single request that includes a 120k-character clinical record + 2k tokens of metadata), how does Redwood count the "billing unit"? Do you chunk/round requests to a fixed token quantum? If so, what is the rounding window?

2) For continuous streaming sessions that keep a large KV cache (multi-step triage flow), is there a session minimum or per-stream floor that could cause unexpected overage during small interactions? Our legal team wants to cap exposure during the pilot.

We attached the draft SOW for context. If you can summarize the approach and propose a pilot-friendly exception (cap/credit or alternate billing method) that would be great.

Appreciate a short note we can share with procurement.

Best,
Alice
Director, AI Platforms
Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-14T12:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how you bill for very long prompts / streaming sessions

Alice — thanks for the clear questions and for sharing the SOW. High-level answers up front, followed by a proposed pilot concession.

Summary: Redwood bills on a per-token basis, where incoming prompt + generated output are converted to tokens and then aggregated into billing quanta. For normal workloads we round usage to the nearest 100-token quantum (i.e., usage is quantized in 100-token buckets). We also maintain a session-level aggregation window so that multiple requests within a short time can be merged for metering efficiencies.

What that means for your two points:
- Very long single-request prompts: those are tokenized and billed as multiple 100-token quanta. Example: a 12,345-token request + 2,100-token response = 14,445 tokens -> rounded to 14,500 tokens billed.
- Streaming sessions & KV cache: we track session IDs. If a session stays warm and we see repeated calls within the aggregation window (default 5 minutes), we collapse those into a single metering bucket to avoid double charging for KV reuse. However, we do have a minimum per-session floor for long-running streams (current default = 1 session unit / 1,000 tokens billed per 24-hour rolling session) which can make very low-activity long-lived connections appear more expensive than many short ad-hoc calls.

Proposed pilot concession (suggested):
- For the 90-day pilot, Redwood will apply a pilot billing mode for the Acme Health SOW: treat "long prompt" single requests > 50k tokens as a single aggregated billing bucket (no per-100-token rounding within that bucket). Effectively we bill the exact token count for that request (no 100-token quantum rounding) up to 200k tokens.
- For long-lived streaming sessions used in the pilot, we will waive the standard per-session floor and instead bill actual aggregated tokens with a monthly cap. If the monthly bill from those streams exceeds $5,000 for accidental rounding/edge cases, Redwood will apply a credit up to $5,000 for pilot months 1–3.

If this concession sounds reasonable I can loop in marissa_cole and karthik_iyer to formalize contract language and update the SOW/pricing table.

Quick Q: do you use a single session id per user or do you create many short-lived session ids? That affects how aggressive we can be on session aggregation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-16T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme Health — pilot billing exception request (need sign-off)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's ask and my proposed pilot concession. High level: they want predictable pilot economics for very long single-request prompts and for long-lived streaming sessions. I suggested:

- No 100-token quantum rounding for single requests >50k tokens (bill exact token count up to 200k).
- Waive per-session floor for pilot streams and cap credits up to $5k/month for months 1–3 if rounding mishits occur.

Items for legal/pricing review:
- Is the "no quantum rounding up to 200k" acceptable operationally (tokens still metered, we just don't round up in that case)?
- Credit logistics: apply as monthly invoice credit, not retroactive refund.
- Define auditability: Acme must provide session_id mapping and sample traces for any disputed months.

I recommend we accept with these guardrails to close the pilot quickly. If you both approve I will send a short SOW amendment and updated pricing table.

—Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear write-up. I am okay with the concession as structured with the following conditions:

1) Pilot mode limited to 90 days from SOW start date.
2) Credit cap applies only to rounding/aggregation edge cases (we will exclude intentional abuse patterns).
3) Any usage that otherwise violates our anti-abuse telemetry (e.g., automated loops creating many session IDs) will be excluded from the concession.

Operational asks for Karthik: please add a small telemetry flag on Acme's account that tags pilot sessions so billing reports can be exported separately. Also add a line to the SOW amendment: "Pilot billing mode subject to telemetry verification and monthly review."

If Karthik confirms feasibility I approve sending the amendment + updated pricing table to Acme.

—Marissa

Confirmations:
- Pilot billing mode (90 days from SOW start): no 100-token quantum rounding for single requests >50k tokens, billed at exact token counts up to 200k.
- Streaming sessions used in the pilot will have the per-session floor waived; usage will be billed by aggregated tokens with a credit cap of $5,000/month for months 1–3 to cover unexpected rounding/aggregation edge cases.
- Acme will provide session_id mapping and 2 sample traces per month if we need to audit usage that exceeds the cap.

Next steps:

2) Sign and return; we will enable "pilot billing" telemetry on your account and share a daily usage export for the first 7 days.
